title: SEAR: Spoofing Evidence-Grounded Audio Reasoning Benchmark for Audio Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.39847v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Audio language models (ALMs) are increasingly used for audio deepfake detection (ADD), yet existing benchmarks assess their verdicts or rationale plausibility without verifying the underlying acoustic evidence. To address this issue, we first introduce spoofing evidence-grounded audio reasoning (SEAR), a four-task AQA benchmark to evaluate ALM-based ADD through acoustic evidence identification and quantification, deepfake detection, and forensic rationale generation. We further propose a bona-fide-based acoustic evidence agent (BAEA), which equips a frozen ALM with controlled acoustic tools under \textsc{fixed} or \textsc{adaptive} evidence-acquisition policies. Experiments with six ALMs reveal a clear gap between plausible rationales and verifiable acoustic evidence reasoning, while BAEA-\textsc{Fixed} improves final verdicts and forensic rationales on both evaluation partitions. translated_title: SEAR：面向音频语言模型的欺骗证据驱动音频推理基准
translated_abstract: 音频语言模型（ALMs）正日益被用于音频深度伪造检测（ADD），然而现有的基准测试仅评估其判定结果或解释的合理性，而未能验证其背后的声学证据。为解决这一问题，我们首先提出了欺骗证据驱动音频推理（SEAR），这是一个四任务的音频问答基准，通过声学证据识别与量化、深度伪造检测以及法证解释生成来评估基于音频语言模型的深度伪造检测。我们进一步提出了基于真实音频的声学证据智能体（BAEA），它为一个冻结的音频语言模型配备受控的声学工具，并采用固定或自适应的证据获取策略。对六个音频语言模型的实验揭示了看似合理的解释与可验证的声学证据推理之间的明显差距，同时BAEA-Fixed在两个评估分区上均提升了最终判定结果和法证解释的质量。受控干预实验进一步表明，误导性证据（原文此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了SEAR基准与BAEA智能体，通过要求验证声学证据而非仅评估解释合理性，揭示了音频语言模型在深度伪造检测中“合理解释”与“可验证证据推理”之间的显著差距，并提升了检测判定与法证解释的质量。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces SEAR, a four-task benchmark for evidence-grounded audio deepfake detection reasoning, along with BAEA, an agent equipping frozen audio language models with controlled acoustic tools, revealing a clear gap between plausible rationales and verifiable acoustic evidence reasoning.
